items.title: Guarding the Gates of Knowledge
items.summary: A recent scroll through social media got me thinking about trust. About half my feed was filled with AI slop that astute users would call out as being machine-generated, often to the embarrassment of the rube who unknowingly spread it and sometimes to the delight of the poster who shared it deliberately because they found it amusing or useful for sowing confusion. Remember the good old days of GPT-3 when we could ask the chatbot anything and it would almost instantly and very confidently spit back a plausible but false answer? That’s when the word “hallucination” as applied to AI answers…

items.title: Q&A: Hey AI, who should I vote for this year?
items.summary: MIT professors Adam Berinsky and Chara Podimata discuss a new project to track how AI chatbots are responding to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.

items.title: From synthetic enterprise data evaluations to real Microsoft Copilot AI confidence
items.summary: Evaluating Microsoft Copilot at enterprise scale requires test data that captures the full complexity of real organizations, yet real enterprise data contains sensitive information that cannot be used for evaluation under any circumstances. The post From synthetic enterprise data evaluations to real Microsoft Copilot AI confidence appeared first on Microsoft Research .

items.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
items.summary: OpenAI will honor a shared robots.txt signal to help website operators communicate their AI training preferences to participating providers.

items.title: A New Map of ‘Empty’ Space Challenges a Tranquil Picture of the Galaxy
items.summary: For decades, astronomers treated the interstellar medium as a static backdrop to the goings-on of the universe. Now, a wave of 3D mapping is bringing the interstellar medium’s dynamic nature into focus.
